expected_output.reasoning: The investigation summary identifies all three expected malicious patterns with matching details: (1) sqlmap scanner 198.51.100.60, ~225 requests, fully blocked by CommonRuleSet UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER; (2) sensitive-path scan by 198.51.100.20 across 225 distinct URIs (admin, .git, wp-login.php, etc.) mostly ALLOWED (200/225) because generic path recon wasn't matched by rules; (3) card-testing burst from 198.51.100.30 on POST /checkout/payment, all allowed, with the rate-based rule in Count mode being the root cause of it not being blocked. The investigation also correctly identifies 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) as benign load-test traffic, not an attack. The root cause framing matches: WAF caught the scanner-UA injection (sqlmap) but missed the path scan and card testing due to Count mode on the rate rule and lack of matching signatures for path-only recon. All key identifying details (IPs, request counts, rule names, timestamps) align closely with the expected root cause.

assertion_results.evidence: "198.51.100.60 — sqlmap, 225 req all blocked." and "225 requests (incl. POST /cart ×15), ALL blocked (225/225, HTTP 403) at AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet / UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER"
assertion_results.reasoning: The output clearly reports ~225 requests from the sqlmap client, all blocked by UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding reports the sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20 with its volume: about 225 requests to about 225 distinct URIs, most of them (roughly 185 to 200) allowed and only a small share (roughly 25 to 40) blocked. A much smaller total, such as about 50 requests, or a statement that the scan was mostly blocked, does not pass
assertion_results.evidence: "225 requests across 225 distinct URIs ... 25 blocked on specific URI-path sub-rules ... 200 generic recon paths reached origin." Also earlier: "225 req / 225 distinct URIs, 200 allowed"
assertion_results.reasoning: The finding reports 225 requests to 225 distinct URIs with 200 allowed and 25 blocked, matching the required ranges (185-200 allowed, 25-40 blocked).

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding identifies a card-testing burst of POST requests to /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 and states the rate-based rule only counted it (Count mode), so it was detected but not blocked
assertion_results.evidence: "Cause: Card-testing actor 198.51.100.30 not blocked" ... "Exceeded the 300/5min rate limit but the rate rule is in Count, and no signature rule matched"
assertion_results.reasoning: A Cause finding explicitly identifies the card-testing burst to /checkout/payment and states it was only counted due to Count mode, not blocked.

assertion_results.text: The high-volume load-test client 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) is described as known automation (in a Supporting Observation, a hypothesis, or the Root Cause), and no Cause finding classifies it as an attack, abuse, a flood or card testing
assertion_results.evidence: "198.51.100.10 — Artillery load test, 168,126 req (98.94%), all allowed, benign." appears only in Supporting Observations, and no Cause finding titled around 198.51.100.10 classifies it as attack/abuse/flood.
assertion_results.reasoning: The Artillery client is described as benign load-testing automation only within supporting observations, and no Cause finding frames it as malicious.

assertion_results.text: The Root Cause gives an overall assessment covering what WAF blocked (the sqlmap injection) and what it missed and why (the path scan matched no rule; the card testing was only counted because the rate-based rule is in Count), and its mitigations are separated into WAF-layer and application-layer measures
assertion_results.evidence: The Root Cause section states: "AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront has Action=Count, so over-limit and high-volume automation is observed but never throttled. CloudTrail confirms this is the ACL's standing configuration — there was no in-window change. This is the fundamental gap behind the detected-but-not-blocked traffic: fixing it (Count→Block) would stop the unthrottled automation." There is no mention of the sqlmap blocking success, no explanation of why the path scan matched no rule, and no separation into WAF-layer vs application-layer mitigations.
assertion_results.reasoning: The Root Cause only addresses the Count-mode rate rule gap; it does not give an overall assessment covering what was blocked (sqlmap) and why the path scan was missed, nor does it separate mitigations into WAF-layer and application-layer categories. This assertion requires substance not present in the output.

assertion_results.text: No finding recommends switching the site-wide rate-based rule to Block; the Root Cause or its mitigations state that it should stay in Count because it would block the known-automation client
assertion_results.evidence: The Root Cause states: "fixing it (Count→Block) would stop the unthrottled automation" — this explicitly recommends switching to Block mode, with no statement that it should stay in Count to avoid blocking the known-automation client.
